headline: No live signal. Full 22-trade ledger still net-negative (-3.7 bps/trade); rolling 11-bet window positive (+6.0 bps) but sample is tiny.
regime_note: BTC is holding near ~$77k, well above the $63-66k range that produced most of the ledger. The last two winning shorts (Aug 21, +48.7 and +16.2 bps) fired into a sharp pullback and dominate the rolling window; that's regime luck, not proven edge.
assessment_md:
**Current state:** No signal is active right now (`signal=0`), so nothing is being risked at this moment.

**The full record:** Across all 22 resolved trades the strategy is net **-3.7 bps per trade** (-82.1 bps total), winning just **31.8%** of the time. That is worse than breakeven and consistent with the prior warning that this signal is marginal and likely not net-profitable after realistic costs.

**What changed vs last time:** Essentially nothing structural. The rolling 11-bet window is still positive at **+6.0 bps net**, but that is almost entirely two large recent short wins on Aug 21 (+48.7 and +16.2 bps) catching a sharp move down from the highs. Strip those out and the picture is ordinary-to-poor. Note the window also uses a 3.0 bps cost assumption, below the ~3.9 bps breakeven — so even that positive figure is flattered.

**What the numbers do and don't tell us:** 22 trades is far too few to conclude anything. Individual results swing from -60.9 to +48.7 bps, so a couple of outliers dominate the average. This is noise, not a verdict. Separately, the offline edge search found **zero survivors** at a 5 bps cost bar on both venues — a real, standing concern about whether any durable edge exists.

**Bottom line:** Underwhelming but not alarming. The full ledger is modestly negative as expected for a marginal signal; the recent bounce is small-sample luck. Keep collecting data — do not read profit into it. No action warranted yet.
